headline: A $5/month Workers Paid plan fee, then per-10ms container billing: CPU on active use only ($0.072/vCPU-hour), memory and disk on the provisioned instance type while it runs. Sandboxes are capped at 4 vCPU / 12 GiB / 20 GB and have no published region pinning. The Workers Free plan cannot run Containers.

compute.cpuBasis: active use only: CPU is billed for the vCPU time the container actually consumes, not the vCPU count provisioned.
compute.ramBasis: allocated: memory is billed on the provisioned memory of the instance type for every 10ms the container runs, busy or idle.
compute.diskBasis: allocated: disk is billed on the provisioned disk of the instance type for every 10ms the container runs.
compute.minimum: No minimum charge or minimum billed duration is published; billing is per 10ms of running time.

openClaw.status: official experimental template in the OpenClaw repository
openClaw.oneClickOrManaged: no one-click button; a documented manual deployment template (scripts/cloudflare) plus Wrangler
openClaw.summary: OpenClaw documents an experimental Cloudflare Containers target: one Worker, one named Durable Object and one Container running the OpenClaw gateway, with Litestream replicating SQLite to R2. It is designed as a single always-on installation (standard-2, max_instances 1). Deployment is manual: clone the repo, create an R2 bucket, build and push an amd64 image to Docker Hub, wrangler deploy, set secrets, then bootstrap once over `wrangler containers ssh`.
steps: Clone openclaw/openclaw and enter scripts/cloudflare; npm install; npx wrangler login.
Create an R2 bucket and an R2 API token; put the account id and bucket name in wrangler.jsonc.
Build the image with docker buildx --platform linux/amd64, push to a public Docker Hub repo, pin the digest in wrangler.jsonc.
npm run check && npm run deploy; then wrangler secret put for the R2 keys and OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN.
Enable ssh temporarily in wrangler.jsonc, redeploy, and run the one-time `openclaw onboard` inside the container over wrangler containers ssh.
Remove the ssh block and redeploy; state survives via the Litestream restore from R2.
openClaw.nonCoderDashboard: No. The dashboard can show the R2 replica tree and container logs, but the deployment needs git, Docker and Wrangler, and first boot needs a shell inside the container.
openClaw.alwaysOn: Yes, by default: OPENCLAW_WEBHOOK_ONLY defaults to false, so the container stays awake and bills provisioned memory and disk continuously. OpenClaw's own estimate is roughly $40-50/month on standard-2 before egress.

evidence.quote: Run one OpenClaw installation behind a Cloudflare Worker and a named Durable Object, with the official OpenClaw image and Litestream replication to R2.
This deployment target is experimental.
The template lives in scripts/cloudflare. It deploys a standard-2 Container with max_instances: 1.
At the published rates, that is roughly 40 to 50 US dollars per month including the plan fee, mostly memory, before egress.
OPENCLAW_WEBHOOK_ONLY defaults to false, which keeps the Container running through idle periods.

deploy.alwaysOnVerdict: The only one of the three with an official always-on recipe for a personal agent: OpenClaw's Cloudflare Containers template keeps one container awake indefinitely and survives restarts via Litestream. It costs the full provisioned memory and disk every hour, and a sleeping (webhook-only) deployment loses its disk, so the always-on mode is the supported one.

notVerified: No account, Worker, container or deployment was created; all behaviour is from documentation.
Snapshot storage is billed somewhere but no rate is published, so it cannot be costed.
The docs conflict on whether outbound internet is on by default; treat it as an explicit per-start setting.
Whether support will raise the 4 vCPU / 12 GiB / 20 GB per-instance ceilings is not published.
